identification: Cut, squashed and folded ring shank (copper-rose colour) with a grey solder lump; no carat stamp visible in either photo. Described as 9ct scrap, 2.6g, unconfirmed. Colour looks coppery, so it could be low-carat or even gilt/base metal; if 9ct at 2.6g it is worth scrap only (about $160 at dealer buy rates).

searches_tried: comps.py (pipeline and work) with 9ct gold scrap ring; WebSearch for 9ct scrap price per gram Australia (dealer buy rates, snippet only); goldprice.org blocked (403). No resale auction comps found for a single unstamped scrap ring; scrap is category-priced by weight so more searching adds little. Gold-api spot read about US$3771 which conflicts with the dealer quote spot of A$5701, so I did not rely on it. eBay sold would not help much because the issue is purity, not market.
viewing_check: Look for a 375/9ct stamp or any carat mark inside the shank (photos show none), and ask for a scratch or acid test and weight. The copper-pink colour could be low-carat, gilt or base metal. Confirm 2.6g on scales.
rate_note: All figures AUD, no conversion. Gowans premium 19.8% extra on hammer.
